text_blocks.snippet: Unifocal breast cancer refers to a condition where a single tumor is found in the breast. It is one of three categories of breast cancer based on the number and location of tumors, the other two being multifocal and multicentric breast cancer. In unifocal breast cancer, there is only one distinct area of cancer cells within the breast tissue.
snippet_highlighted_words: a condition where a single tumor is found in the breast

list.snippet: Unifocal: This term describes a single, isolated tumor within the breast.
Multifocal: This indicates at least two tumors within the same general area of the breast.
Multicentric: This refers to two or more tumors located in different quadrants or areas of the breast.

text_blocks.snippet: While unifocal breast cancer is characterized by a single tumor, the other two types involve multiple tumors, with multicentric tumors being further apart than multifocal tumors. The focality of a breast cancer (whether it's unifocal, multifocal, or multicentric) is an important factor in determining the best course of treatment and prognosis.
